_source: Hand-written for kernel 0.1.0 from the canon (README · docs/rearch/0001–0009 · spine/guide/guide.v0.json · the covenant policy). Every entry is plain, self-contained and under 240 characters — the same contract the old console held its dictionary to. The kernel serves no dictionary door yet; when it does, this file is regenerated from it.
kernel: The one always-running program (orrethd) that holds what must be rigid for a fleet of agents: identity, memory, the rails, the meter, the gate, the watches and the levers. Policy stays with people.
the reference: The same kernel written first in Python (orreth_spine). It runs on port 4601, passes the same conformance fixtures as the Rust kernel, and stays the yardstick the Rust kernel is measured against.
the ground: The kernel's memory: one Postgres database holding every signed record, ask, reply, lease, watch and meter line for a world. One writer ever; nothing is overwritten, corrections sit beside the original.
the rails: The paths every message travels: the ground (Postgres), the invocation rail (RabbitMQ) for work someone must claim, and the events rail (Kafka) for facts anyone may replay. Nothing moves off the rails.
the feed: The live stream the glass listens to: a small notice for every fact as it lands (kind, id, reference). The page fetches the record through a door; the browser never touches a broker.
the outbox: A table on the ground where a fact waits, in the same transaction that made it, until a relay publishes it to the rails. A committed record can never lack its event.
envelope: The one wire shape every ask, reply, fact and tool call wears: canonical bytes, a content hash, who acted for whom (the authority chain) and why (the marker). The same message is the same bytes everywhere.
fact: One thing that happened, signed and kept: a body joined, a reply landed, a lever was pulled. Facts carry pointers and hashes on the rails; the words stay on the ground.
the Record: Every word a body or a person put into the world, kept verbatim and forever with its lineage. A correction is a sibling record; a purge is a governed act that leaves only hashes.
body: Any agent the kernel governs, run as its own process: born from a template, joined through the desk as the same self every life, thinking only through the gateway, serving asks and duties.
resident: A body with a name and a persona — the librarian, echo — the ones that answer you in the chat.
firmware: A body with a function and no persona: the planner, critic, grader, MITL, toolkeeper, stablekeeper and the workspace agents. Same laws as a resident; only the face differs.
the crew: The set of bodies a kernel seats when it lights, declared in one manifest (crew.v0.json): two residents and eight firmware bodies today. Every seat is a process the kernel spawns and governs.
template: A small JSON file that declares a body: its name, nature, persona or function, the graph it runs, the mind it prefers, the tools it may use and the duties it keeps. A body's template hash rides its join.
binding: A JSON file that turns the one workspace-firmware template into a pull's own agent: the prompt, the skills and the tools for the CREW or the MONITOR workspace.
self: A body's or the kernel's permanent identity: an Ed25519 keypair whose public half is its DID. The seed stays on disk under the home; a new identity per run is a defect.
DID: A self's name on the wire — did:orreth:agent:…, did:orreth:kernel:…, did:orreth:person:… or did:orreth:service:… — derived from its public key or, for a person, from their name.
seat: A person's standing at the doors: a capability token the kernel signed after the person proved a code from their authenticator. Every door reads who you are from the seat, never from the page.
the owner: The first person to prove an authenticator on a ground nobody holds. From then on only the owner or a master can enroll another person.
master: A person whose seat can govern: admit a body, restart a parked one, retire a service, and confirm a grave act for someone else from their own window.
the desk: The join desk: the five-status road a body walks to enter a world — pending, challenged, proved, staged, then done or denied. A proven key still waits for a governing seat's yes unless it is the crew or a returning self.
lease: What an admitted body holds: a token chained to the kernel's root that opens the body's own words at the door and nothing more, for thirty days, with a fuel clause in dollars. A lapsed lease reads dormant.
the fuel clause: A body's spending allowance in dollars and the window it renews in, written into its lease and enforced at the gateway. A drained body says so; a refill holds for a person's yes.
the gateway: LiteLLM, run and managed by the kernel: every thought any body has goes through it under the body's own key, and comes back with its cost. Nothing thinks off-meter.
the Stable: The kernel's register of minds (language models): each a stall with a pinned deal — provider, model, price — and an entry in the gateway. The stablekeeper tends it and proposes, never acts alone.
mind: A language model a body may think with, wherever it lives: Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama on your machine, or any OpenAI-compatible base. Assigned to a body for all its work or one class of it.
the meter: The ledger of every thought: which body, which mind, how many tokens, what it cost in dollars. A health check holds it to the gateway's own numbers.
the shelf: The register of every service the kernel governs — tools, MCP servers, stores, sources and minds — on one ladder: registered, versioned, healthy or unhealthy, retired. Retired is rest, never deletion.
tool: Something a body may run: declared as data the kernel reads (name, words, schema, consequence), executed body-side, authorized, journaled and metered by the kernel, which never runs the call itself.
keeper: A firmware body that tends a register on a clock — the toolkeeper the shelf, the stablekeeper the Stable — probing, versioning, and proposing a retire or a re-pin for a person to cut.
consequence: How much an act can change: routine runs at once; consequential holds at the interlock for a person's yes; grave asks for the person's authenticator code and a master's click.
the interlock: The hold in the chat where a consequential act waits: Cancel is the default and has the focus, Yes needs a deliberate click, and the act wears proof L2 when it runs.
proof: How sure the kernel is of who asked: L1 is the ask itself, L2 is an in-chat confirm, L3 is the authenticator's code and a master's click. The demand rises to meet the consequence.
thought: The kind of ask that changes nothing: a question, one answer now. You are the whole loop.
objective: The kind of ask that moves what you asked for: the planner writes the steps, the crew acts, and every step that would change something holds for your yes.
intention: A standing purpose with a stop: the kernel watches for what you named, plans the next objective itself, acts, and reports — a consequence still holds for you. The kernel's own five never end.
the kind of an ask: Thought, objective or intention: read from your words and shown as a chip before you send; one click flips it. The kind decides how far the kernel goes without you.
marker: The typed reason a fact carries — objective, intention, thought, action, observation, improvement… — minted with the fact and linked to its parent, so the lineage of why can be rebuilt from the log.
the Analyzer: The floor hatch of the glass: everything born in the chat grouped by origin — intentions, the objectives under them, in flight and done — read from the ground, never by asking a body.
the one chat: The single conversation with the whole world: a name at the head sends an ask to one body, a time window scopes it, the kind chip says what it is, and every reply names who served it.
session: Your own worldline in the chat: a conversation with its results and artifacts. A new session archives the old one with a short version; nothing is deleted.
the digest: The short version of a session, written from the Record alone and citing what it summarizes.
journey: The soft line under an ask that says where it went, who is fulfilling it and where it was fulfilled — every ask wears one.
THE PANEL: The glass's main window: the kernel drawn as a control room's panel. Geometry is what is declared, light is what is happening, colour is who did it — amber a person, cyan a body, violet the kernel, red a watch or a hold.
organ: One of the six parts the kernel always carries and the panel always draws: the DESK, the GROUND, the GATEWAY, the SHELF, the MONITOR and the ANALYZER.
station: A crew seat on the panel. Solid means seated by its lease, dashed means declared but not seated, amber means the kernel parked it.
the running board: The panel's live tree of work: an intention, the objectives filed under it, the thoughts and actions taken to meet them. Every row opens the Analyzer.
the tape: The panel's newest-first line of facts in words: who asked, who answered, how long it took, which lease lapsed, which lever was pulled and why.
the sill: The bar under the panel with its switches: ARCHITECTURE, OPERATIONS and PERFORMANCE layers, FULL SCREEN, the TOUR, and the doors to the chat, the pulls and the Analyzer.
pull: A workspace that slides in over the glass — CREW or MONITOR today — with its own firmware agent bound to it. Esc puts it back and restores the chat's scope exactly.
the tour: A soft amber line drawn around one part of the live panel at a time, with a plain-words card beside it: what it is, what to try. Say “tour”, or press the switch on the sill.
the guide: What you can say here and what happens: the kernel's own list, served at the /guide door and opened in the glass with “guide”, “help” or “?”.
watch: A named alert on one metric: red while its condition (metric, comparison, threshold) holds, green otherwise. A red watch is an observation the kernel's Resiliency intention acts on.
health check: One sentence that must be true of a world, read from the ground every thirty seconds: every mind answers, the meter and the gateway agree, this cell is sealed, every red is answered…
the harness: The golden cases run against a body's mind on a schedule; a failing run escalates to the chat. From the Rust kernel the run rides the rail to the body.
lever: A governed act the kernel itself can pull through the same door a person would — restart a body, check or restore a service, retire one — declared as data with its consequence and the metrics it remedies.
the remediation rail: What happens when a watch goes red: the kernel reads a dossier off the ground, the planner names one lever from the catalogue, the kernel pulls it, reads the watch again and says what happened.
parked: Held with its evidence, never dropped and never looped. A body that died three times in five minutes is parked; a message the rail carried that was never a valid envelope is parked until a person advances past it.
cell: One universe's physical home: its own kernel self, database and role, benches and topics, bodies and keys, sealed from every other. Cells are worlds.
the seam: The one door two cells that name each other speak through, in messages signed by their kernels' own selves. An ask that names a cell routes home and is answered here.
epoch: A universe's count of homes: it advances when the universe is re-homed to another cell, and the old home refuses to serve a stale one.
MITL: The Master Mind In The Loop: a firmware body that has read the architecture and the covenant, summoned to say who and what an act touches before you decide.
the profile: What this ground knows about you in your own words — name, place, time zone, free claims — labeled by who said it, read first by every body that answers you.
the covenant: The thirteen rules every body wears as a policy sheet and every model coding the kernel holds to; a body without the policy never joins.
the honest boundary: The standing register of what is proven, partial or parked, with the evidence named. A claim not on it is a claim Orreth does not make.
conformance fixture: A language-neutral file of cases both kernels must pass unchanged: given this input, expect these bytes, this hash or this refusal by name. Twenty-six of them are the contract between the two kernels.
the era: The world's version, one number on three faces: the VERSION file, the kernel crate and the reference package. Both health doors whisper it — 0.1.0 today.
